newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine trade unionist warns of pension chaos.
newsitem.headline: Argentine trade unionist warns of pension chaos.

text.p: The former head of Argentina's main CGT labor federation, Gerardo Martinez, warned Wednesday that the government may have to nationalize the recently-established private pensions system.

"The under-financing of the state social contribution system could amount to $9 billion in the next three years, something that could throw the (state) pension system into chaos," Martinez said at the first convention of Argentina's private pension system companies.

"The lowering of employer contributions could risk the advances we have made," he said, warned that if underfunding of the state system continued, "this or another government could nationalize the funds of the private pension system."

Martinez went on to say most of the private funds make short-term investments, giving profits to the fund managers, rather than placing their funds into the "real economy" like small and medium-size firms.
Argentina's private pension system was established in the middle of 1994 and currently manages $4.2 billion in funds for five million members. A state pension system runs parallel to the private one.
